page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores operating at 2.6 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. The CPU exhibits poor single-core performance in stress-ng and weak multi-core performance in both stress-ng and Geekbench. However, memory bandwidth remains average for both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads and writes. Real-world application benchmarks, such as Redis SET operations at 6.25 million operations per second, static web serving at 6.32 GB per second, and Passmark database operations, all fall within the average tier. LLM inference performance is average for small 135M models but drops to poor for medium 7B models.

The primary tradeoff of the E16-8s_v3 is its modest CPU compute capability relative to its massive memory footprint. This makes it a highly cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing, allowing users to avoid paying for unneeded vCPUs just to acquire high memory capacity. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM.
